candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — acknowledge and document practice errors and near misses, printed p.24 / PDF p.28
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — near-miss reporting
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize and report near misses according to organizational safety processes even when no client harm occurs.

options.A: Acknowledge and document the near miss according to the organization's safety-reporting process
options.B: Avoid reporting it because the client was not harmed
options.C: Report it only if the same error occurs again and reaches a client
options.D: Delete any record of the event because near misses are not safety events

candidate.rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan includes acknowledging and documenting practice errors and near misses within Safety and Infection Prevention and Control. A near miss remains safety-relevant even when it is intercepted before reaching the client. Therefore A is the best action. Lack of injury does not eliminate the need to follow the organization's safety-reporting process.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Entry-level RNs should acknowledge and document practice errors and near misses as part of safety practice.
candidate.source_locator: Detailed Test Plan, Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Related Activity Statements from the 2024 RN Practice Analysis, printed p.24 / PDF p.28: acknowledge and document practice errors and near misses
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
candidate.stem: A nurse catches a medication-selection error before the medication reaches the client. No harm occurs. What should the nurse do?
